All processing delays and propagation delays are negligible. Assume that there is no other background traffic over the path and no other additional overhead to transfer the file. Which one of the following is the total time (in seconds) to transfer the file? Note: $1 \mathrm{M}=10^{6}, 1 \mathrm{k}=10^{3}$ $731$ $64$ $8$ $16$

Which one of the following is the total time (in seconds) to transfer the file?

Note: $1 \mathrm{M}=10^{6}, 1 \mathrm{k}=10^{3}$

  1. $731$
  2. $64$
  3. $8$
  4. $16$
codeBlocks:
Bottleneck = min(2 Mbps, 500 kbps, 1 Mbps) = 500 kbps
File size = 4 × 10⁶ × 8 = 32 × 10⁶ bits
Time = 32 × 10⁶ / (500 × 10³) = 64 seconds

questions.questionHtml:
With respect to a TCP connection between a client and a server, which of the following statements is/are true? 

  1. The client and the server use a $2$-way handshake mechanism before the start of data transfer.
     
  2. A TCP connection is half-duplex. 
     
  3. The client and the server can initiate closing of the connection at the same time. 
     
  4. The server cannot initiate closing of the connection before the client initiates.

options.label: A
options.text: The client and the server use a $2$-way handshake mechanism before the start of data transfer.

options.label: C
options.text: The client and the server can initiate closing of the connection at the same time.

options.label: D
options.text: The server cannot initiate closing of the connection before the client initiates.

questions.explanation: Option-$\mathbf{A}$ The client and the server use a $2$-way handshake mechanism before the start of data transfer. Ans : False Reason : Before data transfer, TCP establishes the connection using a $3$-way handshake by exchanging SYN, SYN+ACK, and ACK segments. Option-$\mathbf{B}$ A TCP connection is half-duplex. Ans : False Reason : TCP offers full-duplex service. source: forouzan Option- $\mathbf{C}$ The client and the server can initiate closing of the connection at the same time. Ans : True Reason : Both the ends of TCP connection may send FIN segments at the same time. source: tanenbaum Option- $\mathbf{D}$ The sever cannot initiate closing of the connection before the client initiates. Ans : False Reason : TCP connection release can be initiated by either side (client or server). source: forouzan Answer : $\mathbf{(C)}$ benzene06 answered Feb 16 benzene06 comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or register to add a comment. questions.questionHtml:
​​​​​Consider the following statements:

  1. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) provides a mapping from an IP address to the corresponding hardware (link-layer) address.
  2. A single TCP segment from a sender $S$ to a receiver $R$ cannot carry both data from $S$ to $R$ and acknowledgement for a segment from $R$ to $S$
Which one of the following is CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) provides a mapping from an IP address to the corresponding hardware (link-layer) address.

options.label: B
options.text: A single TCP segment from a sender $S$ to a receiver $R$ cannot carry both data from $S$ to $R$ and acknowledgement for a segment from $R$ to $S$

questions.explanation: Statement $1$: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) provides a mapping from an IP address to the corresponding hardware (link-layer) address. Explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) maps an IP address to a MAC address. When a host needs a MAC address for an IP, it sends a broadcast ARP request. The host with the matching IP responds with a unicast ARP reply containing its MAC address. So, Statement $\mathbf{1}$ is true. Statement $2$: A single TCP segment from a sender S to a receiver R cannot carry both data from S to R and acknowledgment for a segment from R to S. Explanation: A single TCP segment from S to R can carry both data and an acknowledgment (ACK) for a previously sent segment from R to S. This type of acknowledgment is known as a piggybacked ACK, where the ACK is included in the same segment that carries the data. So, Statement $\mathbf{2}$ is false. Answer: $\mathbf{(B)}$ benzene06 answered Feb 27, 2025 benzene06 comment Share Follow 0 reply Please log in or regi

questions.explanation: It is given in the question that, Frame size $=L=3000$ bits Transmission rate $= BW = 2000$ bits$/$second   Transmission time for packet $= T_{t} = \dfrac{L}{BW} = \dfrac{3000 \;b}{2000\;b/s} = 1.5 \;sec$ Propogation time $= T_{p} = 100 \;ms = 0.1 \;sec$ Channel Utilization for Stop $\&$ Wait Protocol $= \dfrac{T_{t}}{T_{t}\;+\;2T_{p}}$ $= \dfrac{1.5}{1.5\;+\;2\times0.1}$ $= \dfrac{1.5}{1.7}$ $= 0.8823$ Channel Utilization in percentage $\mathbf{=88.23\;\%}$ Answer: $(A)$ benzene06 answered Feb 27, 2025 • edited Mar 27, 2025 by benzene06 benzene06 comment Share Follow See all 2 Comments 2 2 Comments reply Vansh462 commented Jan 31 reply Follow flag 'size of acknowledgement is negligible' we won't consider p_ack also negligible Making 1.5/1.6 = 0.9375 As p_ack is always = p_time so your answer is right 1.5/1.7 = 0.8823 ✅ 1 1 reply Share Randy_Rushendran commented Feb 11 reply Follow flag Hey started studing CN today, can you justify your answer? like y

questions.questionHtml:
Consider a network that uses Ethernet and IPv4. Assume that IPv4 headers do not use any options field. Each Ethernet frame can carry a maximum of 1500 bytes in its data field. A UDP segment is transmitted. The payload (data) in the UDP segment is 7488 bytes. 

Which ONE of the following choices has the CORRECT total number of fragments transmitted and the size of the last fragment including IPv4 header?

  1. 5 fragments, 1488 bytes
  2. 6 fragments, 88 bytes
  3. 6 fragments, 108 bytes
  4. 6 fragments, 116 bytes
questions.explanation: MTU $= 1500$ B It is given that IPv4 headers do not use any options field, that means IPv4 Header Size is $20$ B. IP Header Size $= 20$ B So, MTU without IP Header $= (1500 - 20)$ Bytes $= 1480 $ Bytes Now, Payload for UDP Segment is $7488$ Bytes. UDP Header is of $8$ Bytes. So,  Payload for IP datagram $=$ Payload for UDP segment $+$ UDP Header. $= 7488 + 8 = 7496$ Now, fragmenting this Payload for IP Datagram using MTU without IP Header. Total Fragments $= 6$ Last packet data without header $= 96$ Bytes Last packet size with IP Header $= 96 + 20 = 116$ Bytes. So, Total no of fragments are $\mathbf{6}$ and size of last packet including IP Header is $\mathbf{116}$ Bytes. questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements:

  1. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) provides a mapping from an IP address to the corresponding hardware (link-layer) address.
  2. A single TCP segment from a sender S to a receiver R cannot carry both data from S to R and acknowledgment for a segment from R to S.

Which ONE of the following is CORRECT?

 

  1. Both (i) and (ii) are TRUE
  2. (i) is TRUE and (ii) is FALSE
  3. (i) is FALSE and (ii) is TRUE
  4. Both (i) and (ii) are FALSE
questions.explanation: Statement $1$: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) provides a mapping from an IP address to the corresponding hardware (link-layer) address. Explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) maps an IP address to a MAC address. When a host needs a MAC address for an IP, it sends a broadcast ARP request. The host with the matching IP responds with a unicast ARP reply containing its MAC address. So, Statement $\mathbf{1}$ is true. Statement $2$: A single TCP segment from a sender S to a receiver R cannot carry both data from S to R and acknowledgment for a segment from R to S. Explanation: A single TCP segment from S to R can carry both data and an acknowledgment (ACK) for a previously sent segment from R to S. This type of acknowledgment is known as a piggybacked ACK, where the ACK is included in the same segment that carries the data. So, Statement $\mathbf{2}$ is false. Answer: $\mathbf{(B)}$ benzene06 answered Feb 27, 2025 • edited Feb 27, 2025 by benzene06 benzene06 comment Sh

A user starts browsing a webpage hosted at a remote server. The browser opens a single TCP connection to fetch the entire webpage from the server. The webpage consists of a top-level index page with multiple embedded image objects. Assume that all caches (e.g., DNS cache, browser cache) are all initially empty. The following packets leave the user's computer in some order.

  1. HTTP GET request for the index page
  2. DNS request to resolve the web server's name to its IP address
  3. HTTP GET request for an image object
  4. TCP SYN to open a connection to the web server

Which one of the following is the CORRECT chronological order (earliest in time to latest) of the packets leaving the computer?

  1. $\text{(iv), (ii), (iii), (i)}$
  2. $\text{(ii), (iv), (iii), (i)}$
  3. $\text{(ii), (iv), (i), (iii)}$
  4. $\text{(iv), (ii), (i), (iii)}$
questions.explanation: Correct Answer - Option C The standard sequence of operations when trying to reach a server are as follows.  Device checks with local DNS server to identify the destination IP address.  Since HTTP uses TCP network protocol, it has to setup a link with the webserver, hence it sends a syn packet to the server's IP that was resolved using DNS query.  After a TCP connection has been established, The host would request for an index of the webpage using the HTTP GET command.  Based on the Index recieved, Host would make further requests to get the other information that it made the connection for.  Option C would be the best fit for the discussed sequence

questions.explanation: Utilisation of Link = Efficiency Efficiency of Stop and wait protocol is $\eta$ = $\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + \left(\dfrac{2T_{p}}{T_{t\text{}}}\right)}\right)$  = $\left(\dfrac{1}{1 +\left(\dfrac{2d*B}{v*L}\right)}\right)$ where $d$ = link length (distance) , $v$= speed , $B$ = bandwidth (Transmission Rate) and $L$ = packet Length As Efficiency $\eta$  is inversely proportional to distance $d$, So Longer Distance means lower efficiency. As Efficiency $\eta$  is also inversely proportional to Bandwidth $B$, So Higher Bandwidth means lower efficiency. Hence option $B$ is correct. Reference: Computer Networking: A Top Down Approach Book uses Bandwidth and Transmission Rate as same thing https://www.sfu.ca/~ljilja/ENSC835/News/Kurose_Ross/Chapter_1_V7.01.pdf (page 19)

You need to know certain points about OSPF if you are GATE aspirant OSPF is an open standard, not related to any particular vendor. OSPF is hierarchical routing protocol, using area 0 (Autonomous System) at the top of the hierarchy. OSPF uses Link State Algorithm, and an OSPF network diameter can be much larger than that of RIP. OSPF supports Variable Length Subnet Masks (LSM)V, resulting in efficient use of networking resources. OSPF uses multicasting within areas. When sending an identical copy of an earlier datagram, a
host MAY optionally retain the same Identification field in
the copy.

Some Internet protocol experts have maintained that
when a host sends an identical copy of an earlier
datagram, the new copy should contain the same
Identification value as the original.  There are two
suggested advantages:  (1) if the datagrams are
fragmented and some of the fragments are lost, the
receiver may be able to reconstruct a complete datagram
from fragments of the original and the copies; (2) a
congested gateway might use the IP Identification field
(and Fragment Offset) to discard duplicate datagrams
from the queue.

However, the observed patterns of datagram loss in the
Internet do not favor the probability of retransmitted
fragments filling reassembly gaps, while other
mechanisms (e.g., TCP repacketizing upon
retransmission) tend to prevent retransmission of an
identical datagram [IP:9].  Therefore, we believe that
retransmitting the same Identification field is not
useful.
